newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Dec 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)

The Australian Cricket Board will release the Boxing Day Test team this morning. The Australian first-class side, which is to meet the West Indies, is expected to be conservatively predictable with Steve Waugh returning from injury and Greg Blewett moving to opener in the place of the injured Matthew Elliott. Bowler Andy Bichel replaces team-mate Michael Kasprowicz. Page 15.

Steve and brother Mark Waugh clocked up a 159-run partnership to save New South Wales face to ultimately secure a draw against Queensland in yesterday's Sheffield Shield clash in Brisbane. Queensland ran out of time and called it a day when NSW had reached 9-445 - a second innings lead of 86. Page 15.

West Indian Bowler Ian Bishop sliced the cream off the top Victorian batsmen in yesterday's match at Wangaratta, at one stage sitting at 5-52. The visitors took out the match comfortably, winning by six wickets, with Sherwin Campbell taking out the highest score of 112 not out. Page 15.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

An Australian select team smashed the 4 x 100 metre medley relay world record at the Australian short course swimming championships in Melbourne last night. Adrian Radley, Ryan Mitchell, Geoff Huegill and Michael Klim slashed over two and a half seconds fom the 1993 world record set by the US. Page 32.

Australia has taken out the Indira Gandhi Gold Cup, after downing Korea in the women's hockey final 6-2 in New Delhi in India. Alyson Annan's goal scoring skills reinforced the team's win over Korea in this year's Olympic final. Page 31.

Pakistan's cricketers face some hard times on the training field in the lead-up to the new year after a shameful defeat by an innings and 69 runs in a match against Tasmania over the weekend. Tasmania 435, defeated the tourists, 299 and 67. Page 30.
THE AGE

The West Indies could claim last night at least to be standing on solid ground, and perhaps even moving forward following their second win in a row and only the fourth time this tour, defeating Victoria in Wangaratta by six wickets in the weekend's cricket match. Page 3.

Competitors became slightly unnerved in yesterday's Uncle Toby's Ironman series, which moved to New Zealand with near-dire consequences. Six-metre skis were ripped apart as a south-westerly gale at Piha Beach, west of Auckland, whipped up four-to-five metre waves that led even the most iron of competitors - Trevor Hendy - shaking in his speedos. Hendy finished in eighth place and Scott Reeves took out first place. Page 2.

The Melbourne Knights had a 4-0 victory over West Adelaide at Sunshine last night. Although ninth place in Soccer's Ericsson Cup, the Melbourne Knights last night took the chance to experiment on-field as they pushed Joe Simunic from defence into midfield in the second half and used captain Andrew Marth as sweeper. Page 13.
THE HERALD SUN

The new board members of Australian Football League club Western Bulldogs told supporters opposed to the name change (from Footscray) that they would leave the club if they continued to be harassed over the decision. Fans opposed to the name change claim the board rail-roaded the decision without consulting members. Page 86.

A replacement mast for Sydney-to-Hobart favourite Morning Glory is being flown in from Los Angeles so the giant 80-foot maxi will be on the starting line of the Boxing Day race. The A$360,000 carbon-fibre mast broke during a training sail off Sydney Headson Saturday. Page 76.

Michael Bevan conceded that his Test cricket career has been placed under a great deal of pressure as it was scrutinised yet again last night by selectors. Although the multi-talented Bevan scored a half-century in his last Test innings in Sydney as has taken important wickets in both Tests, his place in the Australian side remains under perpetual review from the national selectors. Page 88.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

In arguably the biggest surf in eight years of Uncle Toby's Iron Man competition in yesterday's round at Piha Beach, New Zealand, Scott Reeves of Burleigh Heads overcame serious illness to conquer four-metre waves, treacherous currents and drifting buoys to emerge as the clear favourite to take the Super Series crown with only two events to go. Page 29.

The Australian Jockey Club committee will meet this morning to discuss an application by Jim Cassidy to have his riding licence reviewed. The popular champion jockey was disqualified for three years in April last year by AJC stewards for his involvement in the infamous "Jockey Tapes" affair. Page 29.

Rising Australian welterweight Shannon Taylor reiterated his claim as a genuine contender for Kostya Tszyu' IBF title with a victory by the third round, with three knockouts, over former two-time world champion Jake "The Snake" Rodriguez on Saturday night. Page 33.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
